scenes.tts: Sonic hedgehog falls off with distance from the floor plate. How does a cell turn how much into which neuron?
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Title card: A Code in Two Classes. The gold Shh slope fills the wall, bright at the bottom and pale halfway up.
scenes.narration: Sonic hedgehog falls off with distance from the floor plate. How does a cell turn how much into which neuron?

scenes.tts: A signal that spreads from a source and gives different instructions at different concentrations is called a morphogen.
scenes.visual: Definition card: morphogen. A source with a fading halo around it.
scenes.narration: A signal that spreads from a source and gives different instructions at different concentrations is called a morphogen.

scenes.tts: The answer is written in transcription factors, mostly homeodomain proteins, which set cell identity across the body.
scenes.visual: A homeodomain protein binding DNA. Label: homeodomain transcription factors.
scenes.narration: The answer is written in transcription factors, mostly homeodomain proteins, which set cell identity across the body.

scenes.tts: In two thousand, James Briscoe, Thomas Jessell and colleagues sorted them in chick.
scenes.caption: In 2000, James Briscoe, Thomas Jessell and colleagues sorted them in chick.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Briscoe, Pierani, Jessell and Ericson, 2000.
scenes.narration: In 2000, James Briscoe, Thomas Jessell and colleagues sorted them in chick.

scenes.tts: They asked one question. Does Sonic hedgehog switch the factor off, or switch it on?
scenes.visual: Two buttons on screen: Shh switches it off; Shh switches it on.
scenes.narration: They asked one question. Does Sonic hedgehog switch the factor off, or switch it on?

scenes.tts: Class one factors are switched off by Sonic hedgehog. Each is expressed above a certain height and lost below it.
scenes.caption: Class I factors are switched off by Sonic hedgehog. Each is expressed above a certain height and lost below it.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Class I bars come down from the top of the ventral wall, each stopping at its own height.
scenes.narration: Class I factors are switched off by Sonic hedgehog. Each is expressed above a certain height and lost below it.

scenes.tts: Examples are Pax seven, D B X one and two, I R X three, and Pax six.
scenes.caption: Examples are Pax7, Dbx1 and Dbx2, Irx3, and Pax6.
scenes.visual: Class I bars labelled Pax7, Dbx1, Dbx2, Irx3 and Pax6.
scenes.narration: Examples are Pax7, Dbx1 and Dbx2, Irx3, and Pax6.

scenes.tts: The more sensitive the factor, the higher its border sits. Pax seven is lost at low levels, so it stays in the dorsal half.
scenes.caption: The more sensitive the factor, the higher its border sits. Pax7 is lost at low levels, so it stays in the dorsal half.
scenes.visual: The Pax7 bar stops high, at about the middle of the tube. Label: dorsal half.
scenes.narration: The more sensitive the factor, the higher its border sits. Pax7 is lost at low levels, so it stays in the dorsal half.

scenes.tts: Class two factors are switched on by Sonic hedgehog. They are expressed only below a certain height.
scenes.caption: Class II factors are switched on by Sonic hedgehog. They are expressed only below a certain height.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Class II bars rise from the bottom of the wall, each stopping at its own height.
scenes.narration: Class II factors are switched on by Sonic hedgehog. They are expressed only below a certain height.

scenes.tts: N K X six point one is one. N K X two point two needs the most signal, so it sits beside the floor plate.
scenes.caption: Nkx6.1 is one. Nkx2.2 needs the most signal, so it sits beside the floor plate.
scenes.visual: Class II bars labelled Nkx6.1 and Nkx2.2; the Nkx2.2 bar is short, hugging the floor plate.
scenes.narration: Nkx6.1 is one. Nkx2.2 needs the most signal, so it sits beside the floor plate.

scenes.tts: The names are easy to mix up. Class one proteins are the ones Sonic hedgehog represses.
scenes.caption: The names are easy to mix up. Class I proteins are the ones Sonic hedgehog represses.
scenes.visual: Warning card: class I = Shh represses. Class II = Shh induces.
scenes.narration: The names are easy to mix up. Class I proteins are the ones Sonic hedgehog represses.

scenes.tts: Each border sits at a different height, D B X one's among them. So every stretch between two borders carries its own combination of factors: the cell's address.
scenes.visual: The staggered bar ends line up across the wall, cutting it into stretches.
scenes.narration: Each border sits at a different height, Dbx1's among them. So every stretch between two borders carries its own combination of factors: the cell's address.
scenes.caption: Each border sits at a different height, Dbx1's among them. So every stretch between two borders carries its own combination of factors: the cell's address.

scenes.tts: One more factor completes it. Olig two, a different kind of protein that Sonic hedgehog also induces, marks the motor neuron progenitors.
scenes.caption: One more factor completes it. Olig2, a different kind of protein that Sonic hedgehog also induces, marks the motor neuron progenitors.
scenes.visual: An Olig2 bar appears in one stretch only. Label: Olig2, bHLH protein.
scenes.narration: One more factor completes it. Olig2, a different kind of protein that Sonic hedgehog also induces, marks the motor neuron progenitors.

scenes.tts: Predict. Compare the p three row with the p M N row above it. Which markers differ?
scenes.caption: Predict. Compare the p3 row with the pMN row above it. Which markers differ?
scenes.visual: The domain table on screen. A cursor highlights the p3 row, then the pMN row above it. No cell icon; the rows stay still.
scenes.narration: Predict. Compare the p3 row with the pMN row above it. Which markers differ?

scenes.tts: P M N lacks N K X two point two, the factor that needs the most signal. It has Olig two, and a little Pax six.
scenes.caption: pMN lacks Nkx2.2, the factor that needs the most signal. It has Olig2, and a little Pax6.
scenes.visual: The two rows side by side. Nkx2.2 is marked present in p3, absent in pMN; Olig2 and low Pax6 are marked present in pMN.
scenes.narration: pMN lacks Nkx2.2, the factor that needs the most signal. It has Olig2, and a little Pax6.

scenes.tts: That combination marks the motor neuron progenitors, the domain called p M N.
scenes.caption: That combination marks the motor neuron progenitors, the domain called pMN.
scenes.visual: The pMN row highlights. Label: motor neuron progenitor.
scenes.narration: That combination marks the motor neuron progenitors, the domain called pMN.

scenes.tts: Now compare p M N with p two above it. P two lacks Olig two, and has I R X three.
scenes.caption: Now compare pMN with p2 above it. p2 lacks Olig2, and has Irx3.
scenes.visual: The cursor moves to the p2 row. Olig2 is marked absent in p2, Irx3 present; Pax6 is back at full level.
scenes.narration: Now compare pMN with p2 above it. p2 lacks Olig2, and has Irx3.

scenes.tts: These rows compare neighbouring domains. They do not show a cell changing as it moves.
scenes.visual: Small label under the table: neighbouring domains compared, not one cell moving.
scenes.narration: These rows compare neighbouring domains. They do not show a cell changing as it moves.

scenes.tts: Notice the pattern. At each border, a pair of factors trades places. That pairing returns in chapter five.
scenes.visual: Two border lines in the table flash. At each, two factor names are marked: Nkx2.2 and Pax6 at the lower border, Olig2 and Irx3 at the upper. Tag: chapter 5.
scenes.narration: Notice the pattern. At each border, a pair of factors trades places. That pairing returns in chapter five.

scenes.tts: Now fill the five slots. P zero, p one and p two make V zero, V one and V two interneurons.
scenes.caption: Now fill the five slots. p0, p1 and p2 make V0, V1 and V2 interneurons.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. The five empty stripes fill in, top three first: p0 to V0, p1 to V1, p2 to V2.
scenes.narration: Now fill the five slots. p0, p1 and p2 make V0, V1 and V2 interneurons.

scenes.tts: P M N makes motor neurons. P three, beside the floor plate, makes V three interneurons.
scenes.caption: pMN makes motor neurons. p3, beside the floor plate, makes V3 interneurons.
scenes.visual: The bottom two stripes fill in: pMN to motor neurons, p3 to V3 interneurons.
scenes.narration: pMN makes motor neurons. p3, beside the floor plate, makes V3 interneurons.

scenes.tts: You do not need every name. Three markers serve as landmarks: Pax seven, Olig two, and N K X two point two.
scenes.caption: You do not need every name. Three markers serve as landmarks: Pax7, Olig2, and Nkx2.2.
scenes.visual: Three markers highlighted on the map, top to bottom: Pax7, Olig2, Nkx2.2.
scenes.narration: You do not need every name. Three markers serve as landmarks: Pax7, Olig2, and Nkx2.2.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: a level of signal becomes an address, written as a combination of factors.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Box 3 fills with: level becomes an address. Takeaway on screen.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: a level of signal becomes an address, written as a combination of factors.
